Hi Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Were ramping an LLM-powered code-assistant product and want a proposal for a dedicated pool from Redwood. To get us started, attaching a short telemetry sample (opal_telemetry_sample.csv). The key asks:

- Baseline sizing estimate for a dedicated pool to meet our latency SLOs (p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 300ms)
- Burst handling guidance (we see short bursts during daily syncs)
- Cost/sku tradeoffs (A100 vs H100, quantization options)
- Any recommendations for batching/kv-caching settings and canary rollouts for model upgrades

Quick context from our side (rough):
- Current active users: 18k MAU, 1.2k DAU interacting with assistant
- Typical request patterns: interactive chat (70%) + async batch jobs (30%)
- Observed peak minute-level RPS: 180 (10-min windows), sustained RPS during business hours ~45
- Typical prompt tokens: median 260, median response tokens: 380
- ~20% of requests use streaming token delivery

Can you review the sample and tell us what additional telemetry you need? Wed like a back-of-envelope sizing tomorrow and a more detailed proposal early next week. HubSpot deal: HS-38291 (link in email footer).

Thanks for sending the sample. I pulled the team in (ccd Marissa and Karthik). We can absolutely prepare a BES with recommendations, but a couple of quick clarifying questions to make our initial sizing useful:

1) Sessionization: do you pin sessions to a single backend instance (sticky) or are requests stateless across sessions?
2) RLHF/long-context calls: what fraction of requests use >2k tokens?
3) Peak burst shape: is the 10-min 180 RPS an isolated spike (a few minutes) or sustained through the 10-minute window?

5) Preferred deployment mode: Hosted Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) — affects networking and audit overhead in the proposal

Alex / Lina —

Great details, thanks for the quick template fill. Based on the telemetry and answers, heres our preliminary sizing and recommendations (back-of-envelope to use for procurement conversations):

Summary of telemetry we used:
- Median prompt tokens: 260; median response tokens: 380 -> median total ~640 tokens/request
- Streaming: ~20-25% interactive flows
- Peak short spikes: 180 RPS (3-5m), sustained peak-window average ~95 RPS
- Sticky sessions median ~45s which increases effective utilization of open kernels

Key assumptions for sizing model:
- Model: open-instruct-30B-equivalent (quantization-friendly), inference runtime with KV cache and streaming
- Effective tokens/sec per H100 (int8 w/ optimized kernels): ~38k tokens/s for generation workloads (est.)
- Effective tokens/sec per A100 v4: ~22k tokens/s (est.)
- Average tokens per request for capacity calc: 640 tokens

Sizing math (sustained vs burst):
- Sustained business-hour RPS ~45 -> tokens/s = 45 * 640 = 28,800 tokens/s -> ~1 H100 would cover sustained baseline (38k t/s capacity)
- Short 3-5m spikes at 180 RPS -> tokens/s = 180 * 640 = 115,200 t/s -> ~3 H100s would be needed to cover the spike headroom without queuing
- We include additional buffer for retry ripples and canary headroom: recommended initial pool = 4 H100 GPUs dedicated (sustained baseline + burst buffer), with autoscaler for short-term burst to 8-12 GPUs for extreme events. If A100 only, multiply by ~1.7x (so ~7 A100s baseline + bursts to ~12-14)

Operational recommendations:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for interactive flows (reduces avg tokens generated by ~15-25% depending on prompt patterns)
- Use moderate batching (batch size 4-8) with latency SLO tuned to 250-300ms to avoid tail amplification
- Quantization to int8 for model savings; run a small QA pass for output fidelity on your eval set prior to rollout
- Canary rollout w/ 5-10% traffic and automatic rollback on quality regression triggers

Estimated near-term monthly token throughput (pilot month): assuming 45 RPS sustained, 30 days -> 45 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * 640 ≈ 2.7B tokens -> unit-costs estimate in formal proposal

Next steps:
1) 30-min call Monday 06/14 10:00am PT (confirmed) to walk through the numbers and preferred SKUs (H100 vs A100).
2) Post-call we will produce a short proposal (opal-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf) with detailed pricing, SLA options, and rollout plan.

If this aligns, well also include a short quantization fidelity runbook and a recommended canary traffic split.

Thanks — looking forward to the call
